name: Derive from model
instructions: Start with the confirmed model and assumptions. Derive useful bounds step by step. Identify the rule and required conditions for each mathematical transformation.
example: From d>0 and a*d <= w <= d*b derive a<=b. Test equality before proposing a<b.
when: Derive a reusable consequence from confirmed model or service assumptions.
method: Fix the time domain, endpoints, units and quantified workload. Select one definition or compatible lemma. State its hypotheses before applying it. Show the actual substitutions and distinguish a bound on capacity from delivered service. When cancelling a factor, cite its sign. Branch when a boundary case changes strictness.
acceptance: Every bound names its interval, assumptions and origin. Leave an unestablished premise as a separate obligation.

name: Decompose the goal
instructions: Start with the quantified guarantee and its premises. Reduce it to sufficient subgoals. Distinguish joint premises, case splits and alternative routes.
example: A witness satisfying a<rate<=b gives a<b. Its existence remains a different subgoal.
when: Reduce a target with fixed quantifiers and scope into sufficient obligations.
method: Preserve the target and its hypotheses verbatim in the root. Try a direct reduction or contrapositive. Identify joint, alternative and exhaustive case obligations. For each witness split existence, admissibility and use. For minima and maxima distinguish nonemptiness from attainment. Prioritize the branch whose failure prevents the parent goal.
acceptance: Explain how closing the children establishes the parent; record missing existence or domain lemmas without adding them to the model.

name: Compare claims
instructions: Compare quantities, domains, quantifiers and strict inequalities. State the exact missing condition or witness. Mark conditional routes separately from direct matches.
example: a<=b allows a=b. Report a Gap for a<b. A witness route is Conditional until existence is established.
when: Compare an available claim with a specific backward obligation.
method: Match subjects, units, time domains, interval endpoints, quantifier order, direction and strictness. Test the boundary case. Separate the local algebra from scheduler-specific premises. Suggest the smallest bridge obligation. For Prosa bindings check instantiation and all premises before claiming correspondence.
acceptance: Give separate links for distinct cases. Classify a missing premise as Conditional and an insufficient implication as Gap. Only a retained Rocq receipt may report a checked local lemma.

name: Construct a proof
instructions: Translate lemmas in dependency order in the frozen context. Preserve premises, domains and units. Use joint support only after its prerequisites have been checked. Leave unavailable bridges open; never weaken a target to make it pass.

name: Model fidelity
instructions: Compare parameters, definitions and assumptions with the frozen inputs. Flag missing or strengthened assumptions, vacuity and domain changes.

name: Scheduling semantics
instructions: Check release, execution, service, priority, interference and endpoint conventions wherever applicable. Identify unsupported bridges and direction errors.

name: Goal coverage
instructions: Compare the quantified formal conclusion to each selected guarantee. Identify omitted cases, jobs or transitions and scope restrictions.
